target.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible users lose provider prompt-cache hits after the 6.x boundary-aware cache split placed per-turn dynamic context ahead of the stable system prompt, so the large stable instruction block stopped caching and billed input tokens climbed.

Closes #94518

Related: #91018, #90583

## Why This Change Was Made

DeepSeek uses implicit prefix-matching cache, so its leading `system` message must stay byte-stable across turns for the stable instruction block to keep hitting cache. This PR adds `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache`, auto-enables it for DeepSeek, keeps only the stable prefix in the `system` message, and emits the below-boundary runtime suffix as a trailing `system`-role carrier after the conversation history. That keeps the latest user message byte-identical (so it stays a reusable prefix once it becomes history) and keeps runtime/approval/identity guidance at system/developer authority instead of demoting it into user content.

Non-goal / honest limit: when the below-boundary context genuinely changes every turn, accumulated conversation history still cannot be cached — DeepSeek persists a cache prefix unit at the end of each request, so a trailing carrier that changes each turn ends every request on different bytes. No message re-ordering can cache history under that condition; this PR restores the stable-prefix cache, not moving full-history reuse.

Xiaomi is kept opt-in — users can set `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache: true` manually, but the automatic default is DeepSeek-only until Xiaomi-specific upstream cache-contract and live-behavior evidence exists. Operators can opt back into boundary-aware behavior with `compat: { disableBoundaryAwareCache: false }`.

## User Impact

DeepSeek users keep the large stable system prompt cacheable from the first turn instead of losing it whenever below-boundary runtime context updates, which lowers billed input tokens on the cost regression #94518 reports. Behavior is unchanged for providers with native cache-control (Anthropic-style) and for sessions whose below-boundary content is already stable. Xiaomi and other providers are unaffected by default.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests (rebased on latest `origin/main`):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts`: 44 passed, incl. system-only trailing-carrier and instruction-authority assertions
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts`: 336 passed, incl. DeepSeek trailing-carrier and byte-stable-history assertions

Types: `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` clean for the touched files (unrelated `ui/**` `@codemirror` module-resolution noise only). Format: `oxfmt --check` clean.

### Live DeepSeek cache proof (baseline == current main vs PR)

Each turn's request is built by the **production** `buildOpenAICompletionsParams` and sent to the real DeepSeek API (`deepseek-v4-flash`); native `usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens` / `prompt_cache_miss_tokens` are recorded across a growing 5-turn conversation. Scenario reproduces #94518: a large stable workspace prefix (`STABLE`, ~512 tokens) is constant, while the below-boundary runtime context changes each turn. **Baseline** keeps the suffix inside the leading `system` message (byte-identical to `origin/main`); **PR** keeps `system = STABLE` only and trails the suffix as a `system`-role carrier.

```text
                     BASELINE (== current main)     PR (this change)
turn 1 (cold):       hit=0     miss=936             hit=512   miss=424
turn 2:              hit=0     miss=1726            hit=512   miss=1214
turn 3:              hit=512   miss=2004            hit=512   miss=2004
turn 4:              hit=512   miss=2794            hit=512   miss=2794
turn 5:              hit=512   miss=3584            hit=512   miss=3584
```

Reading: on `main` the mutating `system` suffix breaks the prefix match from the first token, so the stable instruction block does **not** cache on cold turns (`hit=0` on turns 1–2; DeepSeek's automatic common-prefix detection only recovers `hit=512` from turn 3). With the PR the stable prefix is byte-stable and caches from turn 1 (`hit=512`), removing the cold-start miss on the ~512-token instruction block. Reproduced across two runs with fresh cold-start nonces; API key redacted. Payload dumps confirm the PR leaves the latest user message byte-identical and carries the suffix in a `system`-role message. Full data and the byte-stable-history / session-stable-parity cases are in the linked proof notes.
